title: DOTP versus DOTA as Ligands for Lanthanide Cations: Novel Structurally Characterized CeIV and CeIII Cyclen-Based Complexes and Clusters in Aqueous Solutions

synthesis.procedure: 40 mg DOTA (20 μmol) was dissolved in 5 mL H2O and brought to pH ~12 with 1 M NaOH. 82 mg (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6 (30 μmol) was added, causing an immediate pH drop to ~2; the pH was then adjusted to 3 with 1 M NaOH. After about 10 min the light orange solution was centrifuged to remove solids. Large yellow-orange crystals of [Ce6(O)4(OH)4(H2O)8(DOTAH)4] grew spontaneously from the clear solution over one week.

reagents.amount: 1 M, to pH ~12 then to pH 3

synthesis.time: about 10 min before isolation of the solution; crystals over one week

synthesis.vessel_or_method: aqueous mixing followed by centrifuge separation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: centrifuge to remove solids; large yellow-orange crystals grew spontaneously from the clear light orange solution over a week

properties.summary: The cluster shows a strong UV ligand-to-metal charge-transfer band at 277 nm and slowly decomposes in solution without formation of other UV-visible species. Soluble roughly at 2 < pH < 6.

synthesis.procedure: The precursor [CeIII DOTA] was prepared from 19 mg CeCl3·7H2O and 21 mg DOTA in 5 mL deionized water; pH 7 was maintained with 1 M NaOH and the solution was stirred for at least 1 h. A 3 mL sample was diluted with 3 mL of 0.2 M NaCl and acidified to pH 3 with 1 M HCl, then placed in an Ar-bubbled electrolysis cell. A potential of 0.85 V vs Ag/AgCl was applied for 2 h (faradaic efficiency 90%), turning the solution from colorless to orange. Dark orange needle-like crystals of [CeIV DOTA(H2O)] grew within a week by vapor diffusion of acetone (0.5 mL) onto 4 × 30 μL samples in a CombiClover plate.

properties.summary: Electrochemical oxidation of colorless [CeIII DOTA(H2O)]− produces an orange in-cage CeIV complex. A reversible CeIV/III process is reported at E1/2 = 890 ± 10 mV vs Ag/AgCl for in-cage DOTA, but no numerical UV-vis λmax for this solid/complex is tabulated beyond the orange color of the crystals and electrolyzed solution.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared as previously published: 19 mg CeCl3·7H2O and 28 mg DOTP were dissolved in 5 mL deionized water (10 mM each). The pH was adjusted to 9–10 with dropwise 1 M NaOH and the solution was stirred for at least 1 h. Slow diffusion of 1,4-dioxane into a 0.5 mL sample yielded small colorless crystals of [CeIII DOTP(H2O)].
synthesis.time: stirred at least 1 h before measurements
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow diffusion of 1,4-dioxane into 0.5 mL aqueous sample; small colorless crystals

properties.summary: UV-vis spectra of the in-cage CeIII DOTP complex were recorded (Figure 4c) and used as the starting point for spectro-electrochemical 1:1 oxidation to CeIV DOTP at pH 2.2. Paramagnetic 1H NMR peaks of CeIII DOTP were distinguished from diamagnetic CeIV DOTP.

measurements.name: UV-vis spectrum
measurements.conditions: 1 mM CeIII DOTP, pH 7.0 (Figure 4c); spectro-electrochemistry of 2.5 mM CeIII DOTP in 0.1 M NaCl, pH 2.2, 1.0 V vs 3 M Ag/AgCl

synthesis.procedure: Direct reaction of (NH4)2Ce(NO3)6 with DOTP analogously to the CeIII DOTP preparation initially formed soluble CexDOTPy at 7 < pH < 10; the solution darkened from light yellow to dark orange over a few days. Slow diffusion of 1,4-dioxane into the aged solution gave small dark orange crystals of CeIV DOTP. Alternatively, CeIII DOTP solutions were bulk-electrolyzed at pH 2.1–2.3 at 1.0 V vs 3 M Ag/AgCl (about 0.2 V above E1/2) until faradaic efficiency <85% relative to the estimated initial concentration; preparative electrolyses used pH 2.0–2.4 with faradaic yields >85%.

properties.summary: In-cage CeIV DOTP shows a UV LMCT band near 299–301 nm. It is relatively stable for several days at pH > 7 but loses CeIV spectroscopic signatures within two days at lower pH. Spectro-electrochemistry confirms a 1:1 CeIII/CeIV conversion with no intermediate.

synthesis.procedure: Mixing aqueous CeIV ((NH4)2Ce(NO3)6) with DOTP analogously to the 10 mM CeIII DOTP procedure initially formed a soluble species CexDOTPy that remains completely soluble at 7 < pH < 10 and irreversibly precipitates below pH 7 or decomposes above pH 10. The solution color intensified from light yellow to dark orange within a few days as CexDOTPy decomposed to in-cage CeIV DOTP and CeIII DOTP.
